Map guide

Every trout layer, explained.

Turn on any layer in the map’s Layers menu - trout waters, runs, migrations, alpine lakes and more. Here’s what each one means, with a real example.

Stocked Waters

Streams and lakes the state stocks with hatchery-raised trout, from the state stocking reports. Tap a stream to see when it was last stocked and with which species.

Example A local creek that gets rainbow and brown trout every spring before opening day.

Stocking Sections

The exact stretch of a stream where the state releases trout, traced from the stocking list's upper and lower limits - not the whole stream. Pennsylvania only.

Example A creek listed as stocked "from the Route 45 bridge downstream to the mouth" is drawn only along that stretch.

Wild Trout Waters

Streams where trout reproduce naturally - the fish were born in the stream, not raised in a hatchery. The species can be native or one introduced long ago.

Example A mountain creek full of wild brown trout (originally from Europe) is a wild trout water even though browns are not native.

Premier Wild Trout Waters

The best wild trout water in each state - the state's own top classification, based on how many wild trout the stream holds. Each stream keeps the state's name for its class.

Example Pennsylvania's Class A Wild Trout Streams or Wisconsin's Class I Trout Waters.

Designated Trout Waters

Waters a state officially lists as trout water, often with special rules (catch and release, fly fishing only, delayed harvest). Includes wild, stocked and trophy waters.

Example Colorado's Gold Medal Waters, Montana's Blue Ribbon streams, or a state's official trout stream list.

Native Trout Regions

Shaded areas on the map where a trout species that has always lived in that region still survives - fish that were there long before any stocking. These are often remote headwaters inside state forests, wilderness areas and national forests.

Example Brook trout in Pennsylvania's state forests or the Great Smoky Mountains; cutthroat trout in Colorado; Apache trout in Arizona.

Stream Gauges

Live USGS gauges on the map. Tap one for current flow and gauge height, with a chart of the last few days, so you know if the water is high, low or just right.

Example Flow jumps after a storm - check the gauge before you drive.

Special Regulation Waters

Stretches with their own rules - catch and release, fly fishing only, artificial lures only, delayed harvest - from each state’s regulation lists, with the rule on the stream.

Example A delayed-harvest section that is catch and release until June, then opens to harvest.

Trout Population Surveys

Real state electrofishing surveys: how many trout live in a stream, how big they grow and how the population has changed over the years. Included with Pro Annual and Lifetime.

Example A survey that found 195 lb of wild trout per acre.

Steelhead & Salmon Runs

Rivers where steelhead and salmon run, by species, with a month wheel that shows when fish are in the river and when the run peaks.

Example A Great Lakes tributary with steelhead in the river from October, peaking in November.

Saltwater Migrations

Where tarpon, permit, bonefish and striped bass move along the coast through the year, plus flats and artificial reefs.

Example Tarpon arriving off southeast Florida in spring and peaking in early summer.

Alpine Lake Explorer

Thousands of high mountain lakes across the West, with elevation, hike and season - and a 3D view to scout the trail before you go.

Example A high Uinta lake that holds cutthroat once the ice is off in July.

Hot Spots

Top-rated bass, walleye, saltwater and other non-trout waters in every state, each with a live Fish Score for its fish.

Example A Florida lake ranked #1 today for largemouth bass.

How fish get thereBorn in the wild (stream-bred)Born in the wild (stream-bred)

Management focusSupporting natural reproduction and self-sustaining sport fisheriesPreserving original regional genetics and pristine habitats

FAQ

Questions anglers ask.

Is TroutScout free?

Yes. Fish Scores, maps, today’s conditions, hatch charts, Anglers Chat and your catch log are free. Premium ($7.99/month or $34.99/year, with a 3-day free trial) unlocks recent and upcoming stockings, alerts, 7-day forecasts, the Scout Scanner, offline maps and more. Pro Annual ($59.99/year) adds Trout Population Surveys, and Lifetime ($129.99 once) includes everything forever.

Where does the Fish Score come from?

It’s built from live National Weather Service weather, USGS stream flow and water temperature, the time of day and season, recent stockings, hatches in season and today’s angler reports – tuned to each water’s fish. The score on the map is the current hour, and each stream shows its best 3-hour window. It’s a guide to the best times, not a guarantee.

Which states are covered?

All 50 U.S. states have Fish Scores, on 148,000+ streams plus lakes and coastal water. In bass and saltwater states TroutScout scores for the local fish. Stocking, wild and native trout, surveys and regulation coverage depends on what each state’s wildlife agency publishes.

What are Trout Population Surveys?

Real electrofishing surveys from state agencies: how many trout live in a stream (pounds and trout per acre), which species, how big they get and how the population has changed over the years. They’re included with Pro Annual and Lifetime.

Does it work without cell service?

Yes, with Premium. Save any area as an offline map – satellite, dark and terrain maps, 3D terrain, stream lines, access points and your saved pins come with you. Live Fish Scores and weather need a signal.

How do stocking alerts work?

Save a stream and turn on its alert. When the state posts a new stocking for it, you get a notification right away. Premium anglers can turn on alerts for all their streams.

Will other anglers see my fishing spots?

No. Your catch log is private. You choose what to share in Anglers Chat, and you can share a catch without its location.

How do I cancel?

Subscriptions are managed by Apple: open Settings, tap your name, then Subscriptions. Cancel at least 24 hours before a renewal or trial ends and you won’t be charged. Lifetime is a one-time purchase.

Does it work on Android?

TroutScout is on iPhone first. Follow @troutscoutapp for news.
